source.title: Engineering Verifiable Modularity in Transformers via Per-Layer Supervision

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests head ablation effects and argues that the Hydra effect depends on architecture and training: its control shows near-zero effects, while per-layer-supervised models show larger effects. This refines the scope of the claim, but does not directly measure downstream component outputs or compare total effects with the ablated components' direct effects.
record.gate_note: The study reports ablation outcomes for three tasks in two models. Feature-clustering statistics and attention-scaling/steering results are not rows because they do not measure self-repair or the effects of ablation. Claims and results cited from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study zero-ablates two-head groups in layer 5 of two custom 6-layer models and reports only the total change in correct-answer probability. It never measures the heads' direct effect or any downstream component's response. A small total effect in the control could mean the heads matter little, not that they are compensated for. The authors take the Hydra effect as the explanation for the control's small effects; they do not test it. Their results show that their per-layer-supervision method enlarges total ablation effects, which is a result about their own method.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that the authors attribute the control's small ablation effects to Hydra compensation without measuring direct effects or downstream repair, so that attribution is an interpretation, not a result.
record.recipe_differences: Uses head-output zeroing and downstream task-performance changes, as in ablation-based tests of the Hydra effect, but evaluates small custom CASCADE models and grouped heads on three narrow tasks rather than directly measuring downstream repair against a component's direct effect.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome differs between per-layer-supervised PLS and C2 without per-layer supervision. Reported tasks and head groups also differ; the Winograd per-case standard deviation is much larger for PLS than C2.

fits_no_version.finding: In identical CASCADE models, per-layer supervision gives zero-ablation total effects 5–23× larger than the control (e.g. −11.4% vs −2.1% on capitalization). Winograd per-case SD is 6.32% vs 0.63%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training objective (per-layer auxiliary losses) changes the size and spread of head-ablation total effects in small transformers. Whether this reflects reduced self-repair or different head importance is untested.

record.problems: The experiments use custom 6-layer, 6-head CASCADE models trained on grade-school instructional text, and only three narrow tasks. The ablations remove groups of two heads. The paper interprets low behavioral changes as compensation but does not measure downstream component outputs or compare the total behavioral effect with the ablated component's direct effect. The Winograd confidence intervals cross zero.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. The attention-scaling/steering experiment is excluded because it measures the effect of scaling heads, not ablation or self-repair; feature clustering and raw-activation comparisons likewise do not measure the claim.

untested.parts: No layer-level ablation; no measurement of later attention layers' outputs.
No late-MLP analysis of erasure of the maximum-likelihood token.

Head-level compensation is never quantified; there is no direct-effect versus total-effect comparison and no evaluation on the full distribution. Only tiny custom models, two-head groups and narrow tasks are used.
No compensation fraction, per-prompt compensation, or overcorrection is measured; only the spread of total effects is reported.
No mechanism of repair (backup heads, copy suppression, LayerNorm, neurons) is examined.
No comparison of importance scores against direct effects.

record.verdict_notes: All ablated heads (h52–h55) are in layer 5, the final layer of a 6-layer model. Any compensation could therefore come only from the final MLP or LayerNorm, yet none is measured. The models are custom gated-attention dual-stream designs, so even a measured effect would not transfer straightforwardly to standard transformers. The steering and clustering results are rightly excluded.

versions.untested_parts: No single attention layer is ablated, and the study does not measure later attention layers changing their outputs to restore a prediction.
No late-MLP downregulation of the maximum-likelihood token, or its change under earlier-component ablation, is measured.

Tests are on two small CASCADE models and three narrow tasks, not general text across model families and sizes. The intervention removes groups of two heads, not single heads, and the study does not measure the full output distribution or directly compare total effects to the ablated heads' direct effects.

The study reports per-case variation for Winograd ablation effects, but does not measure whether compensation itself varies by prompt or overcorrects relative to a direct effect. Other tasks and prompt sets are not assessed for this pattern.

The study identifies task-associated entity and anchor head groups, but does not test backup heads, copy-suppression heads, final LayerNorm rescaling, or anti-erasure neurons as mechanisms of self-repair.
Heads are ablated by zeroing their output. Mean or resample ablations are not tested.
The study does not calculate or compare ablation-based importance scores against what components do.

rows.subject: PLS model
rows.size_stated: 6 layers, 6 attention heads per layer; hidden dimension 384
rows.stage_stated: trained on grade-school instructional text with per-layer supervision
rows.operation_detail: Zeroed the entity heads h54+h55 and measured change in probability assigned to the correct answer.
rows.measure: Change in probability assigned to the correct answer, Δ = Pablated(correct) − Pbaseline(correct)
rows.note: The sizable behavioral change is reported, but no direct-effect measure is given to determine how much compensation occurred.
rows.check: This is a total ablation effect with no direct-effect baseline, so it cannot show compensation. The ablated heads are in the final layer (layer 5), so only the last MLP and the final LayerNorm are downstream.

rows.subject: PLS model
rows.size_stated: 6 layers, 6 attention heads per layer; hidden dimension 384
rows.stage_stated: trained on grade-school instructional text with per-layer supervision
rows.operation_detail: Zeroed the anchor heads h52+h53 and measured change in probability assigned to the correct answer.
rows.measure: Change in probability assigned to the correct answer, Δ = Pablated(correct) − Pbaseline(correct)
rows.note: The reported behavioral change is not compared with a direct-effect measure.
rows.check: This is a total effect only; there is no direct-effect comparison, so no self-repair measure is possible.

rows.subject: PLS model
rows.size_stated: 6 layers, 6 attention heads per layer; hidden dimension 384
rows.stage_stated: trained on grade-school instructional text with per-layer supervision
rows.operation_detail: Zeroed the entity heads h54+h55 and measured change in probability assigned to the correct answer across cases.
rows.measure: Mean change in probability assigned to the correct answer
rows.note: The positive mean is described as slight interference by the heads, and the wide per-case spread as exposed sensitivity. Compensation relative to a direct effect is not measured.
rows.check: This is the per-case spread of total effects, not variation in compensation. The CI [−0.38%, 3.12%] crosses zero. It cannot speak to V4's claim of partial or overcorrecting compensation.

rows.subject: C2 control
rows.size_stated: 6 layers, 6 attention heads per layer; hidden dimension 384
rows.stage_stated: trained on grade-school instructional text without per-layer supervision
rows.operation_detail: Zeroed the entity heads h54+h55 and measured change in probability assigned to the correct answer.
rows.measure: Change in probability assigned to the correct answer, Δ = Pablated(correct) − Pbaseline(correct)
rows.note: The paper describes this as only 2.1 percent degradation and interprets the control's small ablation effect as compensation; no direct-effect comparison is reported.
rows.check: The reader's 'partial' rests only on the authors calling the small effect compensation. Without a direct effect, a −2.1% change is equally consistent with the heads simply being unimportant.

rows.subject: C2 control
rows.size_stated: 6 layers, 6 attention heads per layer; hidden dimension 384
rows.stage_stated: trained on grade-school instructional text without per-layer supervision
rows.operation_detail: Zeroed the anchor heads h52+h53 and measured change in probability assigned to the correct answer.
rows.measure: Change in probability assigned to the correct answer, Δ = Pablated(correct) − Pbaseline(correct)
rows.note: The study reports a small ablation effect; it does not measure the direct effect of the heads.
rows.check: Same as r4: a −0.3% total effect with no direct-effect measure does not show compensation.

rows.subject: C2 control
rows.size_stated: 6 layers, 6 attention heads per layer; hidden dimension 384
rows.stage_stated: trained on grade-school instructional text without per-layer supervision
rows.operation_detail: Zeroed the entity heads h54+h55 and measured change in probability assigned to the correct answer across cases.
rows.measure: Mean change in probability assigned to the correct answer
rows.note: The authors describe the control distribution as tightly clustered around zero and interpret it as Hydra compensation. The low variation contrasts with the PLS result; direct effects and compensation by prompt are not measured.
rows.check: A tight spread around zero of total effects does not demonstrate compensation. No direct effect is measured, and the CI crosses zero.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: C2 control, on the three tested tasks
reader_labels.reason: The control has small reported changes after head-group ablation, which the authors interpret as compensation; see r4–r6. The results are from narrow tasks and do not establish the broader full-distribution claim.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: PLS model, on the three tested tasks
reader_labels.reason: Ablation effects differ substantially from the control, including an −11.4% capitalization change; the study therefore shows that the outcome depends on architecture and training, not that compensation holds uniformly. See r1–r3.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Winograd task, comparison of PLS and C2
reader_labels.reason: Ablation-effect variation is much larger for PLS than for C2 (standard deviations 6.32% and 0.63% respectively), so the reported prompt-level variation depends on model condition; compensation and overcorrection are not directly measured. See r3 and r6.
